# Universal Scheduling Protocol (USP) — Complete Reference

> USP is an open standard that enables platforms and AI agents to discover, check availability of, and book time-based services from businesses.

Version: 2026-02-21 | Status: Draft | License: Apache 2.0
Website: https://usp.live | Repo: https://github.com/wix-private/universal-scheduling-protocol-spec

---

## Protocol Summary

USP solves the fragmented scheduling landscape. Existing standards (iCalendar RFC 5545, CalDAV RFC 6638, schema.org/Service, OpenActive) are fragmented, lack native payment integration, and were not designed for autonomous AI agent orchestration. USP unifies:

1. Service discovery — types, pricing, policies, availability hints
2. Real-time availability — time slots, capacity, resource scheduling, slot holds
3. Booking lifecycle — create, confirm, reschedule, cancel, waitlist, post-booking events
4. Payment coordination — flexible paths for different commerce protocols
5. Identity and consent — account linking, buyer consent, privacy compliance

## Deployment Modes

USP offers two deployment modes sharing the same domain core:

### UCP-Native Mode
For platforms already supporting the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, https://ucp.dev).
- Scheduling capabilities register in /.well-known/ucp profile
- Paid bookings use UCP's atomic checkout (create_checkout + complete_checkout)
- Infrastructure inherited from UCP: auth, errors, webhooks, versioning
- Single profile at /.well-known/ucp

### Standalone Mode
For platforms wanting a self-contained scheduling protocol.
- Business publishes /.well-known/usp profile
- Payment uses generic payment_context + confirm-payment (works with any checkout system)
- ACP booking extension available for structured checkout
- IETF-native infrastructure: OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749), RFC 9457 errors, RFC 9421 webhooks

## Service Verticals

| Vertical | Description | Examples |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| appointment | 1:1 session between client and provider | Salon, dental, consulting, therapy, personal training |
| group | Group session with limited capacity | Yoga class, workshop, group fitness, cooking class |
| reservation | Hold on a shared resource for a time window | Restaurant table, conference room, venue, court booking |
| rental | Temporary exclusive use of equipment or space | Car rental, studio space, equipment hire, vacation rental |

Custom verticals use reverse-domain notation: com.{vendor}.services.{vertical_name}

## Core Capabilities

### 1. Service Catalog (dev.usp.services.catalog)
Discover what services a business offers.

Operations:
- POST /services/list — List services with filters (type, category, location) and pagination
- GET /services/{service_id} — Get a single service
- GET /services/feed — Incremental catalog feed for aggregators (RPDE-style)
- POST /services/feed/subscriptions — Subscribe to catalog changes

Service schema fields: id, name, description, type, category, duration, pricing, locations, resources, channel, policies, capacity, images, availability_hint

Duration formats: { "fixed": "PT60M" } or { "range": { "min": "PT30M", "max": "PT120M", "step": "PT30M" } }

Pricing models: fixed, hourly, per_person, variable, free

Policies: cancellation (free_cancellation_until, late_fee), rescheduling (max_reschedules, fee), no_show (fee, grace_period), booking_window (min_advance, max_advance, slot_interval), confirmation_mode (auto/manual), payment_timing (at_booking/at_service/deposit_required/free)

### 2. Availability (dev.usp.services.availability)
Query when services are available and hold slots.

Operations:
- POST /availability/query — Query available time slots
  - granularity: "slot" (full slot objects) or "day" (lightweight day summary)
  - Filters: service_id, start_date, end_date, timezone, resource_id, party_size
- POST /availability/holds — Hold a slot (prevents double-booking, TTL: 5-10 min)
- DELETE /availability/holds/{hold_id} — Release a held slot

Slot states: available, limited, waitlist

Caching strategy (tiered):
- Browse tier: day granularity, 2-4 weeks, 5-15 min TTL (calendar view)
- Select tier: slot granularity, 1-2 days, 30-60 sec TTL (time picker)
- Commit tier: hold operation, real-time, no cache (booking flow)

### 3. Booking Lifecycle (dev.usp.services.bookings)
Create and manage bookings through their complete lifecycle.

Status lifecycle: pending → confirmed → in_progress → completed
                  pending → requires_action → confirmed (when payment needed)
                  Any non-terminal → canceled
                  in_progress → no_show

Operations:
- POST /bookings — Create booking (service_id, slot_id, hold_id, buyer, party_size)
- GET /bookings/{booking_id} — Get booking status
- PUT /bookings/{booking_id} — Update mutable fields (buyer, notes)
- POST /bookings/{booking_id}/confirm — Business confirms (manual mode)
- POST /bookings/{booking_id}/cancel — Cancel with reason
- POST /bookings/{booking_id}/reschedule — Move to new slot
- POST /bookings/{booking_id}/confirm-payment — Confirm payment received (Standalone mode)

Webhooks: booking.confirmed, booking.canceled, booking.rescheduled, booking.reminder, booking.completed, booking.no_show

### 4. Discovery Registry (Optional, dev.usp.services.registry)
Centralized business and service search.

Operations:
- POST /registry/businesses — Register business
- POST /registry/search_business — Search businesses by location, category
- POST /registry/search_services — Search services across businesses

## Transport Bindings

### REST Binding (Primary)
- OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec at openapi/usp-rest.json
- Idempotency: Idempotency-Key header (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header)
- Pagination: cursor-based with {cursor, limit, has_more}
- Errors: RFC 9457 Problem Details
- Request signing: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures

### MCP Binding (AI Agents)
- OpenRPC spec at openrpc/usp-mcp.json
- JSON-RPC 2.0 via tools/call envelope
- Methods: usp/services.list, usp/services.get, usp/availability.query, usp/availability.hold, usp/bookings.create, etc.
- Profile advertised via _meta.usp.profile
- Idempotency via _meta.usp.idempotency_key

### A2A Binding (Agent-to-Agent)
- Task-type mapping from USP operations to A2A task types
- Agent Card with usp_profile extension
- DataPart conventions for structured scheduling data
- Session management with TTL-based expiry

### ESP Binding (Embedded UI)
- Embedded Scheduling Protocol for iframe-based booking UIs
- postMessage-based communication (esp.ready, esp.start, esp.complete, esp.cancel)
- Delegation negotiation for partial vs full delegation
- Iframe sandbox: allow-scripts allow-forms allow-same-origin

## Security

All modes:
- HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ required (TLS 1.3 recommended, RFC 8446)
- Webhook signatures via RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures
- Idempotency keys for state-changing operations
- Hold abuse prevention: max concurrent holds, short TTLs, backoff

Standalone mode additionally:
- OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749) with DPoP (RFC 9449) for auth
- Rate limiting (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers)
- CORS headers for browser-based platforms

## Extensions

### Waitlist Extension (dev.usp.services.waitlist)
Extends: dev.usp.services.bookings
Operations: POST /waitlist, GET /waitlist/{id}, DELETE /waitlist/{id}, POST /waitlist/{id}/accept, POST /waitlist/{id}/decline
Status lifecycle: waiting → offered → converted | waiting → canceled | waiting → expired

### Vendor Extensions
Namespace: com.{vendor}.services.{capability}
Must publish spec and schema URLs matching namespace authority.

## Key Design Principles

1. Domain-first: Scheduling logic is universal across deployment modes
2. Payment flexibility: UCP atomic checkout OR generic payment_context
3. IETF-native: References RFC standards directly for security, auth, errors
4. Agent-first: Every operation designed for programmatic consumption
5. Extensible: Vendor extensions via reverse-domain namespaces
6. Real-time: Slot holds prevent double-booking with automatic TTL release
7. Policy-driven: Machine-readable cancellation, rescheduling, no-show policies
8. Versioned: Date-based versioning (YYYY-MM-DD) with negotiation protocol

## Conventions

- Dates: RFC 3339 (e.g., 2026-03-15T09:00:00-04:00)
- Durations: ISO 8601 (e.g., PT60M, PT24H, P90D)
- Currency: Minor units/cents (e.g., 7500 = $75.00), ISO 4217 codes
- Timezones: IANA identifiers (e.g., America/New_York)
- Capability names: Reverse-domain notation (e.g., dev.usp.services.catalog)

## Roles

- Platform: Consumer-facing app or AI agent (discovers, books on behalf of buyer)
- Business: Entity offering time-based services (Merchant of Record)
- Credential Provider: Manages payment instruments (Google Wallet, Apple Pay)
- Payment Service Provider: Processes payments (Stripe, Adyen, PayPal)

## Cross-References

- UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol): https://ucp.dev — USP's companion for product commerce
- ACP (Agentic Commerce Protocol): https://agenticcommerce.dev/ — Extension available for Standalone Mode
- OpenActive: https://openactive.io — Related open booking standard for physical activities
- schema.org/Service: Complementary structured data for web discoverability
